Home/Company journey

From the first offer to an operating company

Build the company around the work.

A business needs more than campaigns. We connect the brand, website, demand, pipeline, product, delivery, communication, customer experience, and evidence. Start with one stage or shape a phased engagement.

Prepare your company brief ↗Explore all services →

8 stages · 6 disciplines · 76 tools · client-owned systems

01 / launch

Define the business

Turn an early idea or an existing business challenge into a clear audience, offer, operating model, and first delivery plan.

02 / launch

Build the brand and digital foundation

Create a consistent identity, a useful website, and the digital journeys a customer needs to understand the company and take the next step.

03 / operate

Create demand and capture enquiries

Connect research, content, paid media, outreach, and landing journeys so attention can become relevant demand.

04 / operate

Run sales and onboard customers

Make qualification, follow-up, proposals, opportunity stages, and customer onboarding visible across the team.

05 / operate

Organize the team and deliver the work

Create structured Jira or Asana workspaces and connect Slack or Discord communication with project ownership, delivery updates, and the systems your team actually uses.

06 / operate

Support customers and grow the relationship

Connect customer portals, service requests, knowledge, approved messaging, and human escalation so customers know how to get help and teams can follow through.

07 / scale

See the performance of the whole company

Bring sales, delivery, acquisition, customer, and management data into a common reporting system with transparent definitions and reliable refresh.

08 / scale

Scale with useful software, automation, and AI

Improve what works, remove repeatable friction, and expand the company through tested software, bounded AI, stronger data, and a clear operating rhythm.

01

Founder launch workspace

02

New market discovery sprint

A researched segment map and a test plan for a company entering a new region or vertical.

  • Customer and market evidence: A research brief, ideal customer profile, buying roles, comparison map, permitted evidence sources, and documented uncertainties.

  • Launch backlog: A prioritized backlog connecting each build item to a business outcome, acceptance checks, client input, and a responsible owner.

operate / team delivery and collaboration

Organize the team and deliver the work

Create structured Jira or Asana workspaces and connect Slack or Discord communication with project ownership, delivery updates, and the systems your team actually uses.

Prepare this stage in your brief ↗
Level 3Explore a focus
Level 4Inspect the detail

Give every project, task, approval, and operational exception a clear owner and place, while keeping communication useful and accessible across locations and time zones.

01

Client delivery control room

A CRM handoff creates a reviewed Jira or Asana project from a template and sends a linked update to the approved Slack channel.

02

Software release workflow

A tracked work item links to GitHub implementation and a reviewed release status, with failure and rollback responsibilities visible to the team.

03

Employee or contractor onboarding

A role-specific checklist tracks equipment or access requests, training material, first tasks, and manager confirmation using client-approved policies.

04

Customer or developer community

A Discord server with purposeful channels, member roles, onboarding guidance, escalation routes, and a named moderation team.

05

Inventory and vendor workspace

An internal tool for approved item requests, stock movements, vendor context, fulfillment status, and exception review.

  • Jira project setup: Selected project configuration, issue types, workflow states, boards, triage queues, permission responsibilities, and reusable delivery templates for the scoped team.
  • Asana work management setup: Projects, tasks, milestones, ownership, dependencies or rules supported by the selected plan, and reusable onboarding and delivery templates.
  • Slack workspace structure: A channel map, naming conventions, access ownership, communication guidelines, scoped notification rules, and approved apps or workflow handoffs.
  • Discord server and community structure: A purposeful server layout, roles and permissions, onboarding guidance, moderation responsibilities, and scoped bot or notification workflows for a team or customer community.
  • Internal operations tools: A role-aware workspace for selected project, inventory, vendor, or service requests with approval queues, audit context, and exception reporting.
  • Delivery operating guide: A task and status dictionary, review rhythm, handoff rules, new-member onboarding checklist, and a practical runbook for maintaining the setup.

01

Company performance cockpit

02

Operational reconciliation queue

  • Review and action rhythm: A weekly or monthly review structure with diagnostic questions, decision records, owner tasks, and a process for correcting inaccurate inputs.

  • Every published measure has a visible definition, population, window, source, and accountable owner.
  • Representative totals reconcile to the approved sources or have explained and owned exceptions.
  • Refresh failures, incomplete inputs, and stale data are visible rather than silently presented as current.
  • The intended audience can find the relevant decision and trace the important values to source evidence.
  • Management reporting and finance workflow software do not provide statutory accounting, audited statements, tax filing, financial advice, or certification.
  • Source systems and client finance owners remain authoritative for accounting policy, tax treatment, and payment decisions.
  • Forecasts and ROI scenarios are assumptions-based planning outputs; the scope states the data, uncertainty, and calculation limits.
